Mary - Album 1: Bloodlines

Which is Witch

"Which is witch?"

[Intro — door bell / footsteps]

“Hey.”

…

Can I help you?

“My family sent some books.”

Yes.

“I think my book got mixed with the books
that were sent with the books
to the place with all the books.”

…

You mean the library?

“Right.”

Wow.

Money really does save time.

[Verse 1]
He walks straight up to the counter
Like the building knows his name
Coat too clean for Ridgefall weather
Face too calm to feel ashamed

Says his family made a donation
Says one book was not meant to go

Okay

What book?

“The book.”

Fantastic.

That narrows it down, you know

All the books your family donated
Are with all the other books
In the building built for keeping—

Wait for it—

books

[Pre-Chorus]
He looks at me
I look at him

Neither one impressed

Then his eyes move past my shoulder

Toward the desk

Oh no.

[Chorus]
Which is witch?
Which one flies?
Which one curses?
Which one lies?

Which one dances under moonlight?
Which one bargains?
Which one bites?

You want your book?
Then name your proof

You think you know the hidden truth?

Come on, rich boy
Take your shot

Tell me what you know—

Or not

[Verse 2]
He reaches for a book on witches
Sitting harmless on the side

Smiles like someone just discovered
Something fun he wants to try

“If I know more about witches
Than you do—

I get my book.”

Excuse me?

I don’t have your book.

“Sure.”

I don’t.

“Sure.”

…

I already hate this man.

[Pre-Chorus]
He flips a page
Then starts to talk

Old European rites
Protective circles
Hearth traditions
Names erased from village sites

Okay

That’s—

Actually obscure.

Huh.

[Chorus]
Which is witch?
Which one heals?
Which one curses?
Which conceals?

Which old stories changed with kingdoms?
Which were rumor?
Which were real?

You know a fact
I know one too

Congratulations
So do I, you—

Wait

Where did you read that?

“Nope.”

Oh, absolutely not.

[Instrumental Break — rapid guitar / keys / handclaps]

[Call-and-response duel]

HIM:
Iron at the threshold—

MARY:
Regional, not universal!

HIM:
Salt across the window—

MARY:
Later folklore, highly doubtful!

HIM:
Belladonna—

MARY:
Poison!

HIM:
Mandrake—

MARY:
Also poison!

HIM:
Silver—

MARY:
Wrong monster!

…

“Not always.”

…

Okay, now you’re just cheating.

[Verse 3]
Now he’s laughing
I’m offended

Mostly because this is fun

No one ever talks about this
Like the subject weighs a ton

No professor lets me argue
No one wants the stranger lore

Most people hear me say “witchcraft”
And immediately find the door

But he knows obscure translations
Contradictions, names and dates

Every answer makes me dig through
Some forgotten scholar’s claims

And suddenly it’s nearly closing
And somehow I’m losing ground

Which is frankly unacceptable

In my own library

In my town

[Build]
One more question
One more round

I can turn this whole thing around

He gives one answer
I don’t know

…

I hate him.

That was good, though.

[Final Chorus — key lift / layered harmonies]
Which is witch?
Which tale survived?
Which got buried?
Which got revised?

Which old warnings became stories?
Which old stories stayed alive?

Human guesses
Broken records
Half a truth in every myth

Maybe nobody knows the answer

Maybe that’s the point of it

Which is witch?
You win tonight

Don’t get comfortable
All right?

[Music drops — softer keys / faint strings]

Fine.

You win.

“So I get my book.”

What book?

…

He laughs.

Actually laughs.

Then shakes his head.

“You can keep it.”

…

Keep what?

“I know you have it.”

I do not have your book.

“Sure.”

I don’t.

“Sure.”

Stop saying sure.

[Outro]

He turns toward the door
Then stops

Looks back

Like he just remembered something

“Oh.”

…

“What?”

“I’m Hansel, by the way.”

…

Hansel.

“Yeah.”

…

I still don’t have your book.

“I know.”

…

[Door bell]

…

I hate rich people.

[CUT]
